title: VALES. II. The physical conditions of interstellar gas in normal star-forming galaxies up to z = 0.2 revealed by ALMA
question: What are the gas density and FUV radiation field in normal star-forming galaxies at 0.03<z<0.2, from [CII]/CO(1-0)/FIR PDR modelling, and does it evolve with redshift?

what.value: [CII] line fluxes and L_FIR, dust temperatures

evidence.quote: We use previously published values of the far-infrared (FIR) luminosity, $L_{\mathrm{FIR}}$

what.value: Literature samples and high-z [CII]/CO/FIR data for comparison

evidence.quote: together with the galaxy samples compared in Fig. 3 of (cite: hailey2010), from where this figure is taken

recipe.method: Gaussian fit to spectrum, collapse cube over nu_obs±FWHM, Gaussian fit
key_parameters: upper limit = 5x RMS at 100 km/s, FWHM 250 km/s

recipe.method: Compare observed L[CII]/LCO with source-function equation varying Tex and tau
assumptions: equal [CII] and CO filling factors; Tex,CO = dust temperature

recipe.goal: Apply adjustments and fit PDR model
recipe.method: [CII] scaled to 70% (or 50%) PDR fraction, CO x2; KDTree search with chi2 minimisation to Kaufman PDR grid to get n and G0
assumptions: each galaxy is a single PDR component; FIR not halved

evidence.quote: average $L_{\mathrm{[C{\textsc{ii}}]}}$/$L_{\mathrm{CO}}$ ratio for our sample is 3500 (median of $\sim$2400) with a standard deviation of 1200
The unadjusted observations yield a mean incident field strength of 2.63$\pm$0.32 and density of 4.00$\pm$0.95

not_stated_but_needed: Exact KDTree grid and chi2 setup
Villanueva et al. in prep products
missing_for_reproduction: Details of CASA reduction in Villanueva et al. in prep
score_reason: Final analysis uses tabulated fluxes and public PDR models, but the imaging details are deferred to an in-prep paper.
rediscovery_reason: Table 1 gives fluxes and the PDR grid is public, so the PDR fitting can be redone; the data are public after the proprietary period.
